Weekend allied-health stepped-wedge trial (Haines et al. 2017, Trial 1)

Source: R/data.R
haines2017.Rd

Analysis extract of Trial 1 of Haines et al. (2017): withdrawal of weekend allied-health services from 12 acute wards in two hospitals, a complete stepped wedge with 7 periods and 2 wards starting in each of periods 2–7. One row per patient episode. Used by Halkiewicz and Alexeev (arXiv:2610.35853) as the application with visible exposure-time heterogeneity; the exposure weights of the IT estimator at the trial's actual cell sizes give an adequacy radius of 0.124.

Usage

haines2017

Format

A data frame with 14,834 rows and 6 variables:

ward

ward identifier (cluster)

site

hospital

period

study period 1–7

start

first period in which the ward was treated (sequence)

trt

1 if the weekend service had been withdrawn (intervention)

acute_los

acute length of stay in days (analysed on the log scale)

Source

Haines TP, Bowles K-A, Mitchell D, et al. (2017). Impact of disinvestment from weekend allied health services across acute medical and surgical wards: 2 stepped-wedge cluster randomised controlled trials. PLOS Medicine 14(10): e1002412, doi:10.1371/journal.pmed.1002412 ; S2 Data, doi:10.1371/journal.pmed.1002412.s002 . Licence: CC BY 4.0 (not covered by the package's MIT licence). Only the six variables above are retained; see data-raw/make_sw_trials.py and inst/DATA_SOURCES.md.

Examples

n <- with(haines2017, tapply(rep(1, nrow(haines2017)), list(ward, period), sum))
starts <- tapply(haines2017$start, haines2017$ward, `[`, 1)
ord <- order(starts, as.numeric(names(starts)))
sw_radius(design = c(2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 0), icc = 0.0709, cac = 1,
          sizes = n[ord, ])
#> [1] 0.1243615
